title: Explicit exponential sums, character sums and sieve bounds
summary: Numerically explicit derivative tests for exponential sums (Kusmin-Landau, second to fifth derivative tests, iterated van der Corput), explicit counts of integer points near curves, explicit Polya-Vinogradov inequalities (Gauss-sum expansion, Pomerance, Lapkova, Frolenkov-Soundararajan), explicit Burgess inequalities for a prime modulus (moment bound, energy count, amplification, McGown and Trevino tables), and explicit sieve bounds (Montgomery-Vaughan Brun-Titchmarsh, Buthe's weighted forms, Ramare-Viswanadham, Greaves, Fan), with every table or finite verification a named hypothesis.

layers.title: carriers, van der Corput's inequality and character-sum identities

targets.name: intervalExpSum
targets.statement: S_f[a,b] = sum over integers n with a <= n <= b of e(f(n)), e(x) the complex value of Real.fourierChar x; a finite sum over Finset.Icc (ceil a) (floor b).

targets.name: vanDerCorput_finite
targets.statement: For integers N, H >= 1 and complex b_1..b_N, with C(h) = sum_{n=1}^{N-h} b_{n+h} conj(b_n) (zero for h >= N): H^2 |sum b_n|^2 <= (N + H - 1)(H sum |b_n|^2 + 2 Re sum_{h=1}^{H-1} (H - h) C(h)). Corollaries: the absolute-value form; |S_f[N+1,N+L]|^2 <= (L + q - 1)(L/q + (2/q) sum_{r<q} (1 - r/q) |S_{g_r}[N+1, N+L-r]|) with g_r(x) = f(x+r) - f(x); and, for real X, Y >= 1, natural 1 <= H <= Y and |b_n| <= 1 on the integers of (X, X+Y], |Y^{-1} sum b_n|^2 <= 4/H + (4/(HY)) sum_{h=1}^{H-1} |C(h)|. The real-part form of ariasdereyna2024 Lemma 6 is not a corollary (enlarging N + H - 1 to 2Y lowers a negative real-part term).

locator.where: Lemma 2.3, lines 324-339; hiarypatelyang2024 Lemma 2.4, lines 96-108; ariasdereyna2024 proof of Theorem 7, lines 405-415 (absolute-value form; Lemma 6, lines 224-227, states a real-part form)

targets.name: charIntervalSum
targets.statement: For chi : DirichletCharacter C q, q >= 1, M integer and N natural, S_chi(M,N) = sum over M < n <= M + N of chi(n), n cast to ZMod q.

api.name: charIntervalSum_add_level

api.name: charIntervalSum_add
api.statement: S(M, N + N') = S(M, N) + S(M + N, N')

api.name: charIntervalSum_level

api.name: norm_charIntervalSum_le
api.statement: for chi != 1, |S(M,N)| <= min(N, q)

tests.name: quadratic_mod3
tests.statement: quadratic character mod 3: S(0,1) = 1, S(0,2) = 0, S(0,3) = 0

tests.name: principal_mod3

targets.name: maxCharIntervalSum
targets.statement: M_chi = maximum of |S_chi(M,N)| over 0 <= M < q and 0 <= N <= q (a finite maximum).

api.name: le_maxCharIntervalSum

api.name: maxCharIntervalSum_inv

tests.name: principal
tests.statement: principal character mod 3: M_chi = 2 but S(0,6) = 4 > M_chi, so the bound needs chi != 1

targets.name: even_symmetry
targets.statement: For chi != 1 even mod q: sum_{n=1}^{q-1-N} chi(n) = - sum_{n=1}^{N} chi(n) for 0 <= N <= q-1, hence M_chi = 2 max_{0<=N<q} |sum_{n<=N} chi(n)|; for every chi != 1, M_chi <= 2 max_N |sum_{n<=N} chi(n)|.

tests.name: principal_even

targets.name: charIntervalSum_primitive_reduction
targets.statement: For chi mod q with conductor q* and primitive character chi*, and r the product of primes dividing q but not q*: S_chi(M,N) = sum_{d | r} mu(d) chi*(d) sum_{M/d < m <= (M+N)/d} chi*(m); hence M_chi <= 2^{omega(r)} M_{chi*} for chi != 1.

tests.name: induced_mod12

targets.name: kusmin_landau
targets.statement: If f has a continuous monotone derivative on [a,b] and theta <= f'(x) - k <= 1 - theta on [a,b] for some theta in (0,1/2] and integer k, then |S_f[a,b]| <= cot(pi theta/2) <= 2/(pi theta).
hypotheses: f C^1 on [a,b] with f' monotone

tests.name: theta_zero

targets.name: kusmin_landau_asymmetric

targets.name: second_derivative_test
targets.statement: If f has two continuous derivatives on [a,b] with 0 < lambda <= |f''| <= Lambda, then |S_f[a,b]| <= (Lambda(b-a) + 2)(1 + 4/sqrt(pi lambda)) + 1.

targets.name: iterated_vanDerCorput
targets.statement: For real X, Y > 0, d >= 1 and integers H_r >= 1 with sum H_r <= Y: |Y^{-1} sum_{X<n<=X+Y} e(f(n))| <= B max(H_1^{-1/2}, ..., H_d^{-1/2^d}, B^{-1/2^d} T_d^{1/2^d}), B = 2 + 2 sqrt 2, T_d the normalised sum of the iterated differences.

targets.name: first_derivative_test_points
targets.statement: If f has a continuous derivative on [a,a+N] with lambda1 <= |f'| <= c1 lambda1, lambda1 > 0, c1 >= 1, then R(f,a,N,delta) <= 2 c1 N lambda1 + 4 c1 N delta + 2 delta/lambda1 + 1 for every delta > 0.

targets.name: huxley_reduction

targets.name: charIntervalSum_gauss_expansion
targets.statement: For chi primitive mod q >= 2: chi(n) tau(chi^{-1}) = sum_b chi^{-1}(b) e(bn/q), hence S_chi(M,N) = tau(chi^{-1})^{-1} sum_{b=1}^{q-1} chi^{-1}(b) sum_{M<n<=M+N} e(bn/q) and |S_chi(M,N)| <= q^{-1/2} sum_{b=1}^{q-1} min(N, 1/sin(pi b/q)).

targets.name: polya_vinogradov_classical
targets.statement: sum_{b=1}^{q-1} 1/sin(pi b/q) < (2q/pi)(log q + log(4/pi) + pi^2/(12 q^2)); hence M_chi < (2/pi) sqrt q (log q + log(4/pi) + pi^2/(12q^2)) for primitive chi mod q >= 2, M_chi < 2^{omega(r)} (2/pi) sqrt q* (...) for nonprincipal chi, and |S_chi| <= sqrt p log p for nonprincipal chi mod a prime p >= 3.

targets.name: polya_vinogradov_pomerance

targets.name: polya_vinogradov_lapkova

layers.title: explicit Burgess inequalities for a prime modulus

targets.name: degenerate_tuple_count
targets.statement: For integers H >= 1, r >= 1 and d >= 2, the number of d-degenerate tuples in {1..H}^{2r} (for every value v, #{i <= r : b_i = v} is congruent mod d to #{i > r : b_i = v}) is at most (2r-1)!! H^r. Route: the count equals E|Z_1 + ... + Z_H|^{2r} for independent uniform d-th roots of unity; d even: perfect matchings; d > r: rearrangements, r! H^r; odd 3 <= d <= r: random rotation and Jensen give (pi/(d sin(pi/d)))^{2r} r! H^r <= (2r-1)!! H^r for r >= 5; (d,r) = (3,3), (3,4): exact counts 6H^3 - 8H^2 + 3H and 24H^4 - 56H^3 + 42H^2 - 9H.

locator.where: the count behind Theorem 1.2; booker2006 lines 506-507 for d = 2

targets.name: burgess_moment_bound
targets.statement: For p prime, chi != 1 mod p, every integer r >= 1 and real B > 0: sum_{x mod p} |sum_{1<=b<=B} chi(x+b)|^{2r} <= (2r-1)!! B^r p + (2r-1) B^{2r} sqrt p. Route: reduce floor(B) modulo p (a full period sums to 0); d-degenerate tuples contribute <= p each (4.1a), the others (m-1) sqrt p by Weil. The source's r <= 9B is not used.

locator.where: Theorem A, lines 57-63 (stated under r <= 9B; proved in trevino2015kth Theorem 1.2); booker2006 displays (28)-(30), lines 494-510, for quadratic chi

tests.name: r1
